# Versions and generated files are bumped and regenerated once, at the end of a deck pull request

- Context: every deck branch edited `PARSER_VERSION`, `ENGINE_VERSION`, `golden.expected.json` and `derive-digest.expected.json` per group, so every merge of `main` conflicted on them and was followed by a merge, regenerate and re-check cycle (the golden test takes about 30 s, the derive-differential test about 17 s, and each round costs agent turns). Issue 282 proposed three steps; this is the first (issue 288), a convention with no code.
- Decision: during a deck build a group neither bumps a version nor regenerates the golden snapshot or the derive digests. It runs the golden test without `UPDATE_GOLDEN` and reads the diff to review its AST changes. After the last group and a merge of `main`, the pull request bumps each version once and regenerates the snapshot and the digests once, in separate commits. A conflict in a generated file is resolved by taking `main`'s file and regenerating it. `AGENTS.md`, `docs/CARD_SUPPORT_PLAYBOOK.md` (step 9) and `.claude/skills/deck-support/SKILL.md` say so. The pull request checks still fail when the generated files differ, so correctness is unchanged.
- Alternatives: a CI job that regenerates and commits (issue 290, left optional because it needs write permissions and can mask an unintended AST change); keeping the per-group bump and merging more often (the conflicts come from the files, not from the timing).
- Consequences: the golden and derive-digest checks of a deck pull request are red until its last commits, and the progress of a build is read from the group checklist, not from those checks; whoever watches the pull request must not regenerate early to turn them green. A version that does not move during a long build can leave cached support reports in a dev browser stale while the build is in progress, which is acceptable because only merged versions ship.
